title: Tomorrow I will…
goal: Make plans, and discover that Slovak has two different ways to talk about the future — one with a helping verb, one with no helping verb at all.
bekal: form future sentences with *budem* + the dictionary form
recognize verbs whose present form already means the future
talk about the weather and make weekend plans

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Plány na víkend
dialogs.intro: Thursday afternoon. Eva and Budi make plans for the weekend.

lines.speaker: Eva:
lines.id: What are you doing this weekend?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: I don't know yet. Probably just staying home.

lines.speaker: Eva:
lines.text: Ideme s kamarátmi do Tatier. Prídeš?
lines.id: We're going to the Tatras with friends. Want to come?
lines.literal: we-go with friends-ins-pl to Tatras-gen. you-will-come?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: I'd love to! But I don't have the right shoes.

lines.speaker: Eva:
lines.text: Zajtra kúpime nejaké. Poznám dobrý obchod.
lines.id: We'll buy some tomorrow. I know a good shop.
lines.literal: tomorrow we-will-buy some. I-know good shop.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Great. And what will the weather be like?

lines.speaker: Eva:
lines.text: Bude pekne, ale v horách bude chladno.
lines.id: Nice, but it'll be cold in the mountains.
lines.literal: it-will-be nice, but in mountains-loc-pl it-will-be cold.

lines.speaker: Eva:
lines.text: V sobotu nie. V nedeľu možno áno.
lines.id: Not on Saturday. Maybe on Sunday.
lines.literal: on Saturday no. on Sunday maybe yes.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Tak sa vrátime v sobotu večer.
lines.id: Then we'll come back on Saturday evening.
lines.literal: so self we-will-return on Saturday evening.

lines.speaker: Eva:
lines.id: Exactly. I'll send you the details.

notes: **Two ways to talk about the future in one dialogue.** *Budem robiť*, *budem čakať*, *bude pršať* use a helping verb. But *prídeš*, *kúpime*, *vrátime sa*, *napíšem* use no helping verb at all — they look exactly like the present, yet they still mean the future. The reason is the topic of the next unit.

**A temporary rule that's enough for now:** verbs with a **prefix** (*pri-, kú-, vrá-, na-*) usually already mean the future in their present form. Verbs without a prefix use *budem*. The rule leaks in places, but it covers most A1 sentences.
**Bude pekne, bude chladno** — weather is expressed with no subject at all. There's no "it" and no "the weather" — just *bude* + an adverb. English has to add *it*: "it will be cold"; Slovak doesn't.

**Pršať means "to rain", one word for the whole event.** *Prší* = it's raining. *Pršalo* = it was raining. *Bude pršať* = it will rain. Notice that it's the only verb in this dialogue that keeps *bude* while talking about the future — because it's imperfective.

**Ďakujem, že…** — how to thank someone for something specific. The word *že* means "that" and is always preceded by a comma in writing. Notice also *si ma pozvala* with the feminine ending: Eva did the inviting, so the ending is *-la*.

grammars.title: Budem + the dictionary form
body: The first way, and the easiest: pair the future form of *byť* with the dictionary form of the verb. Just like English *will*.
after: **Budem on its own means "I will be"**: *Budem doma* (I'll be at home), *Bude tam veľa ľudí* (there will be lots of people there). Without a second verb, it stands alone as "will be".

**The negative merges into *budem***: *nebudem, nebudeš, nebude, nebudeme, nebudete, nebudú*. Notice that this is **different** from the present of *byť*, which uses a separate word, *nie som*. The future goes back to the general rule.

**One verb has its own future form: *ísť*.** Not *budem ísť* but **pôjdem, pôjdeš, pôjde, pôjdeme, pôjdete, pôjdu**. Learn it separately — it's used every day, and *budem ísť* sounds wrong straight away.

grammars.title: Present forms that already mean the future
body: The second way, and one with no equivalent in English: some Slovak verbs **cannot** be used for the present. Their present form automatically means the future.
after: **The difference isn't time but completion.** *Budem písať list* = I'll spend time writing a letter (the activity). *Napíšem list* = I'll finish the letter (the result). Both talk about the future; what differs is whether the focus is on the process or on getting it done.

**That's why perfective verbs have no present.** You can't be "in the middle of finishing" — once it's finished, it's already past. That's why the present form jumps into the future; there's nowhere else for it to go.

**For now, just recognize the pattern**: the prefixes *u-, na-, pre-, z-, za-, pri-, vy-* usually mark a perfective verb. The whole system comes in full in the next unit — the hardest unit in this book, and the one that opens the most doors.

blocks.text: Notice that weather almost always uses **sentences with no subject**: *je pekne*, *prší*, *sneží*. There's no word for "it" or "the weather" — the verb stands on its own. English must add *it*; Slovak doesn't.

blocks.title: Four very different seasons
items: Slovakia has four distinct seasons. Summer can reach 35°C in Bratislava, winter drops to −15°C in the mountains, and snow in the Tatras lasts from November to April.

For readers arriving from warmer climates, two things often come as a surprise: **the sun sets at four in the afternoon** in December, and **it's light until nine in the evening** in June. That's a five-hour difference, and the body needs time to adjust.

head: Sentence
English
rows: What are you going to do …?
I have to ask at home first.

blocks.text: **Nechceš ísť …?** — Slovak often invites with a **negative question**, and it actually sounds more polite, not less. *Nechceš kávu?* = "Would you like some coffee?" It takes time to get used to if you're used to hearing a negative as a refusal.

blocks.title: The Tatras: a must-see
items: The **Vysoké Tatry** (High Tatras) are the smallest alpine mountain range in the world — only 26 kilometers long — but their highest peak reaches 2,655 meters (Gerlachovský štít). You can see them in a single weekend.
*Štrbské Pleso*, *Hrebienok*, and *Skalnaté pleso* can be reached by rack railway or cable car, so you don't have to hike to enjoy the views.
One serious warning: the weather there changes within minutes, and the marked trails are closed from November 1 to June 15. Bring a jacket even if it's thirty degrees in Bratislava.

exercises.prompt: Put into the future with budem.
Put the words in the right order.

answers: Čo budeš robiť cez víkend? — Ešte neviem. Asi budem doma. — Aké je počasie? — Bude pekne, ale v horách bude chladno. — Nebude pršať? — Napíšem ti.
Budem robiť. — Budeš čítať. — Bude pracovať. — Budeme variť. — Budete čakať. — Budú spať.
